PullRequest.Title: chat: install Agent Host MCP servers from a form in the Customizations editor

For #346688

## Context

Installing an MCP server from the Customizations editor with an Agent Host harness (for example Copilot CLI) asked for everything one step at a time: a quick pick for the connection, one for each value, one for each secret, and then a confirmation dialog. The dialog repeated the server name as "Destination" and listed internal configuration field names. Once installed, the server appeared in the MCP Servers list under its registry ID (`io.github.chromedevtools/chrome-devtools-mcp`) instead of its name.

## What changes

**One page instead of quick picks and a dialog.** Installing an MCP server now opens a page inside the Customizations editor, in place of the current page. It shows what will be installed (server, and its command or endpoint), the fields the server needs grouped by what they configure, and **Install** and **Cancel**. A server that needs nothing shows the same page without fields, which replaces the confirmation dialog. Cancel, Escape, or navigating elsewhere cancels the installation.

**Fewer wrong questions for local packages.** The questions come from the runtime's install plan, which reads some registry entries literally. The Agent Host now corrects them against the registry entry it has already downloaded and verified:

- A flag with no value (such as `-d`, or `--from` ahead of a fixed value) is written as it is rather than asked for as text.
- A repeatable argument written as a single `{variable}` takes one value per line, and is optional unless the entry requires it.
- If a fixed flag is followed by a repeatable argument that was left empty, the flag is left out too.
- A package the host cannot write is refused before the page opens, not after it is filled in.

**Friendly names in the MCP Servers list.** A server the active session reports is named after its installation record, and search finds it by either name. For a configured server whose key is shaped like a registry name, the provider looks the name up in the MCP registry in the background, so the name survives a reload.

## How it is built

- `McpServerInstallForm` is the page. It renders all text from the plan as plain text.
- `ICustomizationInstallationConfigurationService` lets the install provider ask for answers without knowing the editor. The visible Customizations editor registers itself as the presenter; with no presenter the installation is cancelled.
- The provider's quick-pick flow is removed. Skill and plugin installations and all removals still confirm in a dialog.

## For reviewers

- **Registry lookup.** Configuration keys shaped like a registry name are sent to the MCP registry, including ones added by hand, and such a server gets the registry's name. Nothing is sent when the Gallery is turned off.
- **Dropping a flag is a heuristic.** It applies only when the next argument is a repeatable positional one with no values.
- **A flag with a description is still asked for as text**, and an optional single value inside a template is still required. Both are left as they were.
- **One existing test changed meaning:** a value the entry has no place for is now refused when the page is requested rather than at Install.
- **Remote servers are unchanged**: the runtime applies those answers itself.

## How to test

1. Open **Customizations → MCP Servers → Browse** with the Copilot CLI harness.
2. Install a server that needs no input. Expect the page with a summary, Install and Cancel, and no dialog.
3. Install a local server that takes arguments or environment values. Expect one page with all fields; submitting with a required field empty shows the error under that field.
4. After installing, the MCP Servers list shows the server's name, and searching by that name or by the registry ID finds it.

Component Explorer fixtures cover the states: `chat/aiCustomizations/mcpServerInstallForm/*` and `chat/aiCustomizations/aiCustomizationManagementEditor/McpServerInstallPage` and `McpServerInstallReviewPage`.

Validation run on the branch after merging `main`:

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- `scripts\test.bat --run` for `copilotCustomizationInstallations.test.ts`, `agentHostCustomizationMarketplaceInstallProvider.test.ts`, `mcpServerInstallForm.test.ts`, `aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts` and `mcpListWidget.test.ts`: 366 passing
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed TypeScript files and `pnpm run stylelint` on the new stylesheet: passed
- Component Explorer error check on the install form, install page and MCP Servers tab fixtures: 32 rendered without errors

The form was also exercised by hand in a Code OSS Agents window against a local registry. The friendly-name change is covered by unit tests only.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load Agent Host installation inventory and resolve friendly names, including reloads and registry replacement
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Plugin inventory and SDK installation inventory must finish before the installation snapshot is available. The added registry lookup is explicitly fire-and-forget; inventory does not await registry responses. A successful batch subsequently requests one inventory refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read plugin inventory, then installation inventory; the latter issues parallel SDK skill-receipt, MCP-receipt, and MCP-configuration reads, with conditional recovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One plugin-inventory call and one installation-inventory call per refresh, not per configured server. SDK list issues three parallel reads; recovery is conditional and bounded by installation kind. A successful registry-name batch adds one refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same inventory calls already ran on binding and customization changes; the registry-result-triggered refresh is new.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial inventory reads gate snapshot availability; the refresh after name resolution is background work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve registry-shaped configured MCP names to registry metadata using HTTP GET requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For N distinct uncached MCP names without catalogue metadata, one resolver invocation launches N independent lookup pipelines. Each tries available name endpoints sequentially, normally succeeding on the first; redirects can add a slash probe. No ID endpoint is supplied. There are no server requests when the registry manifest is unavailable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agent Host inventory did not perform these presentation-name registry lookups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the inventory critical path. A batch publishes names only after all its pipelines settle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Buffer HTTP response bodies, parse JSON and convert registry metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per successful endpoint response; scales with fetched metadata bytes. Gallery parsing applies its existing response-size guard and 30-second per-request timeout, although the native fetch implementation buffers the body before the gallery guard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These response allocations were absent from Agent Host presentation-name resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background lookup processing, not awaited by inventory.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct registry-shaped configured names lacking catalogue metadata, deduplicated across a batch and cached across sessions owned by the provider; typically a user's configured MCP-server collection rather than registry search results.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Inventory plugin and installation reads are sequential at provider level; three SDK inventory reads run in parallel. Registry resolution uses Promise.all across distinct missing names, sequential endpoint fallbacks per name, and no application-level global limiter; actual HTTP transport scheduling is browser-controlled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Found and definitive NotFound results are remembered for the registry lifetime. Pending requests and transient failures receive a five-minute retry timestamp, suppressing immediate duplicate reads. Retries require another inventory read, not a periodic timer. Registry replacement swaps the map and stale responses cannot publish a refresh. Policy-session creation is separately coalesced and its live session is reused.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the changed invocation through gallery endpoint resolution and native fetch, plus the inventory refresh consumer and cache states.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Configured-name counts, response sizes, registry latency and browser connection scheduling are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: The change adds linear background metadata I/O for its naming feature. Warm keys avoid that I/O, one batch does not perform per-name inventory refreshes, and inventory remains independent of registry latency. No high-confidence pathological amplification beyond the feature's lookup work was established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install a configured local MCP package from the Customizations editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Authentication/workspace trust, host preparation and any existing card retrieval precede the form. Submission validates fields, then one host apply writes the configuration. The new package writability check runs during preparation before presenting the form.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare an installation through the Agent Host and SDK planning; after confirmation send one apply and one SDK MCP configuration add.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One preparation and at most one apply per user installation. Transport choices and individual fields do not each issue an apply or configuration write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same preparation and apply boundaries surrounded sequential quick-input prompts and a confirmation dialog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Preparation gates form display; apply gates installation completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download and verify a URL-backed MCP card; embedded cards use their existing bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The existing preparation reads one card shared by its package/remote choices; the added writability check processes the already-parsed package and makes no additional download.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Preparation already downloaded URL cards and verified the digest before constructing configurable choices.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A small transport-choice collection and the package's declared arguments, environment fields and supplied repeated values.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Choice normalization and writability checks are synchronous on the host. A form submits its selected choice once; the provider never retries ambiguous apply operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The parsed verified card is reused by the new correction and writability checks. Cold SDK policy-session creation is shared; warm operations reuse the policy session. There is no new per-field network cache or lookup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced preparation, parser-only writability checking, form answers and host configuration writing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings or unusually large real-world package manifests were available.
Scenarios.Verdict: The additional preflight performs local transformation/parsing per choice, not extra boundary operations. No concrete performance regression found for normal package manifests.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install a remote MCP server or confirm an input-free MCP installation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing planning and any runtime preparation precede presentation. The user completes or confirms one form, then the provider sends one apply. For configured SDK-owned remotes, runtime preparation and apply remain sequential after answers are collected.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send selected values/secrets once to host apply; SDK-owned remote configuration uses mcp.prepareInstall followed by mcp.applyInstall. Host-written direct-card remotes use mcp.config.add.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected transport's answers and one apply per installation, independent of the number of fields. Input-free reviews still apply without answers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same runtime preparation/apply or configuration-add operations ran after quick inputs and/or a confirmation dialog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runtime operations gate completed installation; replacing prompts does not move additional runtime operations onto the path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Format an input-free command preview and construct the selected transport's answer payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One preview per review and one selected-answer payload per submission; repeated values scale with their submitted line count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The dialog serialized command arguments/environment and the quick-input flow constructed an equivalent selected-answer payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous work before form display or apply.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One installation, a few transport choices, and its values/secrets or command arguments.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One visible configuration page is owned by an editor; a newer request replaces and disposes the previous page. SDK preparation and apply retain their existing ordering.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No per-keystroke host requests or additional card downloads are introduced. Existing client/policy-session reuse is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both configured and review-only branches were traced to their apply calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime operation duration is external to this diff and was not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: The UI replacement preserves boundary cardinality and does not create per-field calls or resubmit apply operations. No reportable performance regression found.

Scenarios.Scenario: Edit fields, switch transport, resize, cancel or navigate away from the installation form
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Form construction creates choice sections synchronously. Input validation, multiline measurement and scrollbar scanning run on the renderer; cancellation removes the page and resolves collection without applying.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Transport choices and declared fields, generally a few choices with a handful or tens of fields; repeated-field text controls validation and mirror measurement work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Renderer work is synchronous; ResizeObserver triggers layout. No network, filesystem, SDK calls or subprocess launches are made by editing or transport switching.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each choice keeps its controls and entered values for the form lifetime. Multiline inputs are measured on layout. The page, observer, controls, event subscriptions and cancellation listener are disposed together on close, replacement, hidden editor or navigation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: reviewed all form code, InputBox layout, scrollbar scanning and editor-owned DisposableStore/MutableDisposable cleanup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DOM/layout timings were not profiled; no evidence established a self-sustaining resize loop or realistically excessive field count.
Scenarios.Verdict: All-choice construction and geometry measurements are bounded by the current form, with explicit teardown. No high-confidence eager-work, layout-thrashing or retention regression found.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and search active-session-only MCP servers using installation display names
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing list filtering reads the in-memory installation snapshot, resolves optional names and renders matching entries.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Active-session-only server count and search-text length; each server performs at most one installation-target lookup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous renderer filtering and Map lookups. The changed helper does not schedule asynchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: findByTarget uses the snapshot's prebuilt MCP-ID Map. Rendering does not fetch metadata; provider updates replace the existing snapshot through the established observable path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced createBuiltinActiveSessionMcpEntries to the snapshot implementation and list filtering caller.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Server counts and render timings were not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: The richer label adds constant-time indexed lookup per server and local text matching, not quadratic installation scans or per-row I/O. No reportable regression found.

Analysis.Summary: Inspected the complete 17-file inventory and every diff page, then completed the performance-review pass with targeted caller, cache, lifecycle, SDK, HTTP and rendering investigation. No high-confidence actionable performance regressions or concrete performance-regression fixes qualified for submission. Static review only; runtime magnitude was not measured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
